Title: Async HTTP Fetcher
Code:
import asyncio
from typing import Optional

class FetchResult:
    def __init__(self, url: str, status: int, body: str):
        self.url = url
        self.status = status
        self.body = body

async def fetch_url(url: str, timeout: float = 5.0) -> Optional[FetchResult]:
    try:
        reader, writer = await asyncio.wait_for(
            asyncio.open_connection("example.com", 80),
            timeout=timeout,
        )
        request = f"GET / HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: example.com\r\n\r\n"
        writer.write(request.encode())
        await writer.drain()
        data = await asyncio.wait_for(reader.read(4096), timeout=timeout)
        writer.close()
        return FetchResult(url, 200, data.decode(errors="replace"))
    except (asyncio.TimeoutError, OSError) as e:
        print(f"Error fetching {url}: {e}")
        return None
Explain: asyncio.wait_for adds a timeout to any awaitable.
writer.drain() ensures buffered data is actually sent.

Title: Async Semaphore Rate Limiter
Code:
import asyncio
import time
from typing import Any, Callable, Coroutine
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

@dataclass
class RateLimitStats:
    total: int = 0
    succeeded: int = 0
    failed: int = 0
    durations: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def avg_duration(self) -> float:
        return sum(self.durations) / len(self.durations) if self.durations else 0.0

class RateLimiter:
    def __init__(self, max_concurrent: int = 5, delay: float = 0.1):
        self._sem = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)
        self._delay = delay
        self.stats = RateLimitStats()

    async def execute(self, coro_fn: Callable[..., Coroutine], *args: Any) -> Any:
        async with self._sem:
            self.stats.total += 1
            start = time.monotonic()
            try:
                result = await coro_fn(*args)
                self.stats.succeeded += 1
                return result
            except Exception:
                self.stats.failed += 1
                raise
            finally:
                self.stats.durations.append(time.monotonic() - start)
                await asyncio.sleep(self._delay)
Explain: asyncio.Semaphore limits how many coroutines run concurrently.
The finally block ensures delay and timing happen even on failure.
